video.explanation: The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) took effect across Europe in May 2018. It aims to protect the privacy and personal data of EU citizens and imposes strict guidelines on how businesses handle and process personal information.

video.text: What is the service level agreement for two or more Azure Virtual Machines that have been manually placed into different Availability Zones in the same region?
video.explanation: Azure provides an SLA of 99.99% for two or more Virtual Machines placed across different Availability Zones in the same region. Note: 99.95% is the SLA for an Availability Set; 99.99% is for Availability Zones (per Azure VM SLA documentation).

video.text: Which of the following is considered a downside to using Capital Expenditure (CapEx)?

options.text: It does not require a lot of up front money
You are not guaranteed to make a profit
You must wait over a period of years to depreciate that investment on your taxes
You can deduct expenses as they occur

video.explanation: Capital Expenditure (CapEx) involves large, upfront investments in assets that are depreciated over time. This means businesses must wait years to fully depreciate the investment for tax purposes, which can be a financial burden in the short term.

video.text: Azure Cloud Shell allows access to the Bash and Powershell consoles in the Azure Portal
video.explanation: Azure Cloud Shell provides access to both Bash and PowerShell consoles directly within the Azure Portal, allowing users to manage their Azure resources without needing to install or configure any local tools.

video.text: What does it mean if a service is in General Availability (GA) mode?

options.text: You have to apply to get selected in order to use that service
Anyone can use the service but it must not be for production use
Anyone can use the service for any reason
The service has now reached public preview, and Microsoft will provide support for it

video.explanation: When a service is in General Availability (GA) mode, it means the service is fully released to the public, is stable, and can be used for production environments. Microsoft provides full support for GA services.

video.text: Which of the following scenarios would Azure Policy be a recommended method for enforcement?

options.text: Add an additional prompt when creating a resource without a specific tag to ask the user if they are really sure they want to continue?
Require a virtual machine to always update to the latest security patches
Allow only one specific roles of users to have access to a resource group
Prevent certain Azure Virtual Machine instance types from being used in a resource group

video.explanation: Azure Policy is designed to enforce governance rules and ensure compliance with organizational standards. Preventing the use of specific Azure Virtual Machine instance types in a resource group is an example of how Azure Policy can be used for enforcement by restricting resource configurations or types.

video.text: What does ARM stand for in Azure?
video.explanation: ARM stands for Azure Resource Manager. It is the deployment and management service in Azure that enables users to manage and organize Azure resources, define and deploy resources using templates, and apply policies for resource governance.

video.text: What types of files can a Content Delivery Network speed up the delivery of?
video.explanation: A Content Delivery Network (CDN) can speed up the delivery of various types of static content, including images, videos, JavaScript files, and PDFs. CDNs cache these files in multiple locations around the world, reducing latency and improving load times for users.

video.text: What is the maximum amount of Azure Storage space a single subscription can store?
video.explanation: Azure Storage offers virtually unlimited storage capacity for a single subscription. While there are practical limits for individual storage accounts (such as 5 PB for a general-purpose v2 storage account), the overall storage capacity across all accounts in a subscription can scale to meet extremely high demands.

video.text: What is the concept of being able to get your applications and data running in another environment quickly?
video.explanation: Reproducible deployments is the concept of ensuring that applications and data can be quickly and consistently deployed in different environments. This approach involves automating the deployment process, using tools like infrastructure as code (IaC), to make environments easily replicable.

video.text: Besides Azure Service Health, where else can you find out any issues that affect the Azure global network that affect you?

options.text: Install the Azure app on your phone
Each Virtual Machine has a Resource Health blade

video.explanation: In addition to Azure Service Health, you can check Resource Health for individual resources, like Virtual Machines, to monitor their health and status. This provides insights into any issues that might affect specific resources, including network issues, outages, or degradation.

video.text: In what way does Multi-Factor Authentication increase the security of a user account?

options.text: It requires the user to possess something like their phone to read an SMS, use a mobile app, or biometric identification.
It doesn't. Multi-Factor Authentication is more about access and authentication than account security.
It requires users to be approved before they can log in for the first time.

video.explanation: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) enhances security by requiring multiple forms of verification from the user. This typically includes something the user knows (password), something they have (a phone for SMS or an authentication app), or something they are (biometric data). This makes it much harder for unauthorized users to gain access to the account.

video.text: Which of the following elements is considered part of the "perimeter" layer of security?

options.text: Keep operating systems up to date with patches
Locks on the data center doors
Separate servers into distinct subnets by role

video.explanation: The perimeter layer of security focuses on protecting the network's outer boundary by preventing unauthorized access. Firewalls are a key component of this layer, as they help filter traffic and block malicious connections before they reach internal systems.

video.text: What is the benefit of using Powershell over CLI?
video.explanation: PowerShell offers object-oriented scripting, deeper integration with Windows environments, and the ability to handle complex automation tasks more efficiently than the Azure CLI. It also supports advanced functionalities like working with .NET objects, making it more powerful for administrative tasks.

video.text: Azure charges for bandwidth used "inbound" to Azure.
video.explanation: Azure does not charge for inbound data transfers (data coming into Azure). However, outbound data transfers (data leaving Azure) are typically charged based on usage.

video.text: What is the benefit of using a command line tool like Powershell or CLI as opposed to the Azure portal?
video.explanation: Using PowerShell or Azure CLI allows you to automate repetitive tasks, deploy resources consistently, and manage Azure environments more efficiently. This is especially useful for Infrastructure as Code (IaC), scripting, and large-scale deployments.

video.text: What two types of DDoS protection services does Azure provide? Select two.
video.explanation: Azure provides two levels of DDoS protection. DDoS IP Protection is a cost-effective solution designed for small and medium-sized businesses, offering protection for individual public IP addresses. DDoS Advanced Protection, previously known as DDoS Protection Standard, is an enterprise-grade solution that provides broader network-level protection.

video.text: What Azure product allows you to autoscale virtual machines from 1 to 1000 instances, and also provides load balancing services built in?
video.explanation: Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets (VMSS) allow you to automatically scale virtual machines from 1 to 1000 instances based on demand. They also include built-in load balancing to distribute traffic efficiently across instances, ensuring high availability and performance.

video.text: Within the context of privacy and compliance, what does the acronym ISO stand for, in English?
video.explanation: ISO is a globally recognized organization that develops and publishes standards for various industries, including privacy, security, and compliance. In the context of Azure, ISO certifications help ensure that cloud services meet international security and data protection standards.

video.text: Where do you go within the Azure Portal to find all of the third-party virtual machine and other offers?

options.text: Choose an image when creating a VM

video.explanation: In the Azure Marketplace, you can find third-party virtual machine images, applications, and other offers that are available for use within your Azure environment. It's the place to discover and deploy a wide range of resources provided by Microsoft and its partners.

video.text: Select the way(s) to increase the security of a traditional user id and password system?

options.text: Require longer and more complex passwords.
Do not allow users to log into an application except using a company registered device.
Use multi-factor authentication which requires an additional device (something you have) to verify identity.
Require users to change their passwords more frequently.

video.explanation: To enhance the security of a traditional user ID and password system, it's essential to use stronger passwords, ensure access is restricted to trusted devices, and implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) to verify identities with something the user has, like a phone or token.

video.text: How many regions does Azure have in Brazil?
video.explanation: Azure has two regions in Brazil: Brazil South and Brazil Southeast. The Brazil South region is located in São Paulo State, while the Brazil Southeast region is situated in Rio de Janeiro. These regions provide cloud services with local data residency to help meet regulatory and compliance requirements in Brazil.

video.text: What is the concept of Availability?

options.text: The percentage of time a system responds properly to requests, expressed as a percentage over time
A system that can scale up and scale down depending on customer demand
A system must have 100% uptime to be considered available
A system that has a single point of failure

video.explanation: Availability refers to how consistently a system remains operational and accessible. It is typically measured as a percentage over a given period (e.g., 99.9% uptime). High availability ensures minimal downtime, allowing users to access the system reliably.

video.text: Why is Azure App Services considered Platform as a Service?

options.text: You give Azure the code and configuration, and you have no access to the underlying hardware
You are responsible for keeping the operating system up to date with the latest patches
You can decide on what type of virtual machine it runs - A-series, or D-series, or even H-series
Azure App Services is not PaaS, it's Software as a Service.

video.explanation: Azure App Services is a Platform as a Service (PaaS) offering because it allows developers to deploy applications without managing the underlying infrastructure. Azure takes care of hardware, networking, and OS updates while developers focus on writing and configuring their code.

video.text: What is a benefit of economies of scale?

options.text: The more you buy of something, the cheaper it is for you
Prices of cloud servers and services are always going down. It'll be cheaper next year than it is this year.
Big companies don't need to make a profit on the first product they sell you, because they will make a profit on the second
Big companies don't need to make a profit on every sale

video.explanation: Economies of scale refer to the cost advantages that businesses gain as they scale up. In cloud computing, this means that as more customers use cloud services, the provider can reduce costs per unit, passing on savings to customers through lower prices or better services.

video.text: Which free Azure security service checks all traffic travelling over a subnet against a set of rules before allowing it in, or out.
video.explanation: An Azure Network Security Group (NSG) is a free security service that controls inbound and outbound traffic for a subnet, network interface, or virtual machine based on a set of security rules. It helps protect Azure resources by filtering network traffic before allowing or denying access.

video.text: What does it mean if a service is in Public Preview mode?

options.text: Anyone can use the service for any reason
You have to apply to get selected in order to use that service
Anyone can use the service but it must not be for production use
The service is generally available for use, and Microsoft will provide support for it

video.explanation: When an Azure service is in Public Preview, it means that anyone can access and test it, but it is not yet recommended for production environments. Microsoft continues to refine the service based on user feedback before making it Generally Available (GA).

video.text: Each person has their own user id and password to log into Azure. But how many subscriptions can a single account be associated with?
video.explanation: A single Azure account (user ID) can be associated with multiple subscriptions without any fixed limit. This allows users to manage different environments, such as development, testing, and production, or separate billing for different projects or teams.

video.text: In which US state is the East US 2 region?
video.explanation: The East US 2 Azure region is located in Virginia and is one of Microsoft's primary cloud regions in the eastern United States. It provides a wide range of cloud services with low-latency access for users in the region.

video.text: Windows servers use "remote desktop protocol" (RDP) in order for administrators to get access to manage the server. Linux servers use SSH. What is the recommendation for ensuring the security of these protocols?

options.text: Ensure strong passwords on your Windows admin accounts
Do not allow public Internet access over the RDP and SSH ports directly to the server. Instead use a secure server like Bastion to control access to the servers behind
Disable RDP access using the Windows Services control panel admin tool
Do not enable SSH access for Linux servers

video.explanation: Exposing RDP and SSH directly to the internet increases the risk of brute-force attacks and unauthorized access. Instead, using Azure Bastion or a VPN with private access provides a more secure way to manage servers without exposing these ports to potential threats.

video.text: Approximately how many regions does Azure have around the world?
video.explanation: Microsoft Azure operates over 60 regions worldwide, providing a comprehensive global infrastructure to support customers across various locations.

video.text: If you are a US federal, state, local, or tribal government entities and their solution providers, which Azure option should you be looking to register for?

options.text: Azure is not available for government officials

video.explanation: Azure Government is a cloud solution designed specifically for US federal, state, local, and tribal government entities and their solution providers. It provides highly secure, compliant, and isolated cloud environments that meet government-specific regulations.

video.text: What is an Azure resource?

options.text: A physical device in an Azure datacenter.
A software component that provides a service.
A logical entity that represents a cloud resource.

video.explanation: In Azure, a resource is a logical entity that represents an instance of a cloud service, such as virtual machines, storage accounts, databases, or networking components. Resources are managed within resource groups and can be organized using tags and policies for better governance.

video.text: What is the principle of least privilege in the context of Azure RBAC?

options.text: Assigning the "Owner" role to all users.
Disabling user accounts when they are not in use.
Granting users the maximum amount of access necessary to perform their job duties.
Granting users the minimum amount of access necessary to perform their job duties.

video.explanation: The principle of least privilege (PoLP) ensures that users, applications, and services only have the minimum permissions needed to perform their tasks. In Azure Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), this helps reduce security risks by limiting unauthorized access to resources.

video.text: Which is the lowest-cost storage redundancy option?
video.explanation: LRS (Locally Redundant Storage) is the lowest-cost Azure storage redundancy option because it keeps three copies of data within a single datacenter in the same region. Unlike GRS or ZRS, LRS does not provide protection against datacenter failures, making it the most cost-effective but least resilient option.

video.text: Which of the following can be considered a benefit of using the cloud regarding security? Select all that apply.

options.text: Ability to disable security measures such as encryption for specific applications or uses

video.explanation: Cloud providers like Azure continuously update and patch their systems to protect against vulnerabilities, adhere to compliance standards like ISO, GDPR, and FedRAMP, and provide centralized security management and monitoring through tools like Microsoft Defender for Cloud.

video.text: Which compute type is designed to package and deploy applications along with their dependencies, ensuring consistent behavior across different environments?
video.explanation: Containers are designed to package applications along with their dependencies (libraries, runtime, and configuration) into a single, lightweight unit. This ensures consistent behavior across different environments. Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) and Azure Container Apps are popular Azure solutions for managing containers.

video.text: Which Azure Storage access tier is optimized (including for cost) for data rarely accessed and must be stored for at least 180 days, with flexible latency requirements?
video.explanation: The Archive access tier in Azure Storage is optimized for data that is rarely accessed and must be stored for at least 180 days to avoid early deletion fees. It offers the lowest storage cost but has higher retrieval latency, making it ideal for long-term backup, compliance, and archival storage.

video.text: Which of the following is an example of a serverless computing service?
video.explanation: Azure Functions is a serverless computing service that allows you to run code without managing infrastructure. It automatically scales based on demand and charges only for execution time, making it ideal for event-driven applications, background tasks, and automation.

video.text: Fill in the blank: ___ is a cloud-based file sharing service that allows you to access your files from anywhere using standard SMB or NFS protocols.
video.explanation: Azure File Storage is a cloud-based file sharing service that allows users to access files from anywhere using standard SMB (Server Message Block) or NFS (Network File System) protocols. It enables fully managed file shares that can be mounted on Windows, Linux, and macOS environments.

video.text: Who typically owns the IT infrastructure in the cloud computing model?

options.text: The vendor such as Microsoft Azure or Amazon AWS

video.explanation: In the cloud computing model, the cloud provider (vendor) owns and manages the IT infrastructure, including servers, storage, networking, and data centers. Clients rent or subscribe to these resources instead of purchasing and maintaining their own infrastructure.

video.text: A large financial institution with strict compliance requirements and a need to maintain control over sensitive data would be best suited for which cloud model?
video.explanation: A Private Cloud is ideal for organizations like a large financial institution with strict compliance requirements and a need to maintain control over sensitive data. The cloud infrastructure is dedicated exclusively to that organization, offering greater control, security, and customization.

video.text: Why is it beneficial to organize Azure resources into resource groups?
video.explanation: Resource groups in Azure help organize and manage related resources, making it easier to deploy, monitor, and control access to them as a single unit. They allow for logical grouping, consistent access control, and bulk operations.

video.text: What is the primary purpose of Microsoft Entra Conditional Access?

options.text: To implement granular access controls based on specific conditions.
To provide multi-factor authentication for all users.

video.explanation: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access is a security feature that allows organizations to control access to resources based on specific conditions such as user location, device status, risk level, and application being accessed. It helps enforce Zero Trust security.

video.text: By design, when an entire Azure region fails as it may during a natural disaster in that region, where do some Azure services automatically fail over to?

options.text: Its region pair, which is at least 300 miles away in the same geography
Another region, which is usually located in another geography
There are no Azure services that fail over if its region were to fail
Most regions fail over to US East

video.explanation: Azure follows the Region Pair strategy, where each region is paired with another region at least 300 miles away within the same geography. In the event of a regional failure, some services automatically fail over to their paired region, minimizing downtime and data loss.

video.text: Can subscriptions be nested?
video.explanation: Azure subscriptions cannot be nested. Each subscription exists as a separate entity under an Azure account (tenant). However, multiple subscriptions can be managed under a single Azure tenant using management groups.

video.text: What is the primary purpose of Availability Zones in Azure?

options.text: To provide redundancy and fault tolerance
To offer discounts for customers in certain regions
To provide access to Azure services in specific geographic locations

video.explanation: Azure Availability Zones are physically separate locations within an Azure region, each with independent power, cooling, and networking. They help ensure high availability and fault tolerance by allowing workloads to be distributed across multiple zones.

video.text: Which of the following are required in order to create an Azure Virtual Machine? Select all that apply.
video.explanation: To create an Azure Virtual Machine, you must have an Azure subscription to provision resources, a resource group to manage and organize the VM, and a name to identify it. While a virtual network is typically needed for connectivity, Azure can automatically create one for you if none is specified.

video.text: What is the maximum number of instances that can be in a virtual machine scale set?
video.explanation: Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets (VMSS) can support up to 1,000 instances for standard images. However, if you use custom images, the limit is 600 instances. VMSS allows automatic scaling of virtual machines to handle varying workloads efficiently.

video.text: Which of the following is an example of a PaaS offering from Azure?

options.text: Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory)

video.explanation: Azure App Service is a Platform as a Service (PaaS) offering that allows developers to deploy and manage web applications without worrying about the underlying infrastructure. It provides built-in scaling, security, and integration with DevOps tools.

video.text: What is the primary benefit of using containers for deploying applications to Azure?
video.explanation: Containers package applications along with their dependencies, ensuring they run consistently across different environments, such as development, testing, and production. This makes them highly portable and reduces compatibility issues when deploying applications.

video.text: Queue storage can be used when two programs need to communicate. Which type of communication is this best suited for?
video.explanation: Azure Queue Storage is best suited for asynchronous communication, where messages are placed in a queue and processed later. This allows decoupling between components, enabling scalability and reliability without requiring both programs to be online at the same time.

video.text: How does a defense-in-depth model improve overall security?

options.text: By eliminating the need for user training.
By reducing the need for security updates.
By making it more difficult for attackers to breach multiple layers of security.

video.explanation: The defense-in-depth model improves security by implementing multiple layers of protection, such as firewalls, encryption, access controls, and monitoring. This layered approach ensures that even if one security measure is bypassed, others are still in place.

video.text: Which Azure service can be used to create a highly available application across multiple Availability Zones?
video.explanation: Azure App Service, Azure Storage, and Azure Virtual Machines all support high availability across multiple Availability Zones. VMs can be deployed across Availability Zones for redundancy, App Service provides built-in high availability, and Storage offers geo-redundancy.

video.text: What does redundancy mean in the context of Azure?

options.text: Implementing failover to a secondary data center in case of a disaster.
Monitoring system health to detect and prevent issues.
Using a single instance of a resource to avoid failures.
Having multiple copies of a resource to ensure availability.

video.explanation: Redundancy in Azure refers to maintaining multiple copies of a resource, such as data or virtual machines, to ensure high availability and fault tolerance. This helps protect against failures by providing backup systems that can take over if the primary resource fails.

video.text: There is a well-defined division of responsibilities in the cloud. The cloud vendor is typically responsible for the physical and network security of the cloud. Who is typically responsible for the security and protection of customer data in the cloud?

options.text: The cloud provider and the customer are both equally responsible
It's really difficult to say anyone is responsible for it
The cloud provider, such as Microsoft Azure or Amazon AWS

video.explanation: In the shared responsibility model, the cloud provider is responsible for securing the infrastructure (physical security, networking, hypervisor). However, customers are responsible for securing their own data, applications, and configurations within the cloud, including access controls and encryption.

video.text: What is a key benefit of using Azure Budgets?
video.explanation: Azure Budgets helps organizations monitor and control their cloud spending by allowing them to set budgets for their Azure usage and costs. It provides alerts when spending approaches or exceeds predefined thresholds, ensuring better financial management.

video.text: How does Azure Policy help manage Azure resources?

options.text: By optimizing resource utilization and cost
By providing real-time alerts for security threats
By defining rules that govern resource configuration and usage
By automatically scaling resources based on demand

video.explanation: Azure Policy helps organizations enforce compliance by defining and applying rules that govern the configuration and use of Azure resources. It ensures that resources adhere to company standards and regulatory requirements by automatically auditing and remediating non-compliant resources.

video.text: What is the primary purpose of Azure B2B collaboration?

options.text: To provide identity and access management for cloud-based applications.
To allow guest users from external organizations to access your organization's resources.
To provide identity and access management for internal users.
To enable customers to purchase products and services directly from your organization's website.

video.explanation: Azure B2B (Business-to-Business) collaboration allows organizations to securely share applications and services with external users, such as partners, contractors, and vendors. It enables seamless access while maintaining control over security and compliance.

video.text: What type of scaling typically involves adding more resources to a pool of existing resources?
video.explanation: Horizontal scaling, also known as "scaling out," involves adding more instances of resources (e.g., virtual machines, containers, or application instances) to distribute the workload. This approach improves availability and load balancing while maintaining performance as demand increases.

video.text: Which cloud pricing model is often used for applications with predictable workloads and long-term requirements?
video.explanation: Reserved instances allow you to commit to a specific amount of cloud resources for a longer term (typically one or three years) in exchange for significant cost savings. This pricing model is ideal for applications with predictable workloads and long-term stability requirements.

video.text: Which of the following is a key benefit of using Microsoft Entra Domain Services?

options.text: It provides a managed domain service in the cloud without the need to manage on-premises domain controllers
It simplifies the management of on-premises Active Directory
It is only suitable for small-scale deployments
It is a replacement for Azure Active Directory

video.explanation: Microsoft Entra Domain Services (formerly Azure AD Domain Services) offers managed domain services like domain join, group policy, and LDAP, allowing organizations to use traditional Active Directory features without deploying and maintaining domain controllers in the cloud.

video.text: Many years ago, your company licensed software that requires access to the Windows Registry to run. There is currently no option to run the app without the ability to write to the Registry. Which of the following is the only option for running this app in the cloud?
video.explanation: Since the application requires access to the Windows Registry, it must run on a full Windows OS environment where registry modifications are allowed. IaaS (such as Azure Virtual Machines) provides full control over the operating system, enabling applications that depend on system-level access to function properly.

video.text: How does the consumption-based model help businesses manage their IT costs?

options.text: By aligning costs with actual usage

video.explanation: The consumption-based model (also known as pay-as-you-go) allows businesses to only pay for the resources they use, rather than making large upfront investments or long-term commitments. This model helps manage IT costs by providing flexibility and eliminating the expense of unused capacity.

video.text: Your company runs most of its data and applications on-premises and only uses the cloud when it needs to temporarily scale for more resources. For instance, it has 18 virtualized servers on-premises and can scale up to another 18 virtual machines in Azure if needed. What is this usage of the cloud called?
video.explanation: A hybrid cloud setup combines on-premises infrastructure with cloud resources, allowing businesses to scale their workloads as needed. The company primarily runs on on-premises servers but temporarily uses Azure for additional capacity, which is a typical example of hybrid cloud usage.

video.text: How does high availability help businesses avoid financial losses?
video.explanation: High availability ensures that critical systems remain operational with minimal downtime, allowing businesses to continue serving customers, processing transactions, and maintaining productivity. This prevents financial losses caused by service outages that could disrupt revenue streams.

video.text: Unexpectedly, a celebrity posts a glowing review of your product. Your website receives a huge spike in traffic and orders, and handles it well because your cloud platform automatically added additional resources as required and turned them off when no longer required. This property of your application is known as
video.explanation: Scalability is the ability of a system to automatically adjust resources to handle increased or decreased demand. In this case, your cloud platform automatically added resources to handle the traffic spike and then scaled them down when demand decreased, ensuring smooth performance without unnecessary costs.

video.text: What is the primary purpose of Azure Data Box?

options.text: To create and manage Azure virtual machines
To build and deploy web applications in Azure
To transfer large amounts of data to and from Azure

video.explanation: Azure Data Box is a physical device that helps businesses securely transfer large volumes of data to and from Azure, especially when network-based transfer is too slow or impractical.

video.text: One of the benefits of cloud computing is that you can create a set of virtual machines that can automatically scale to add more resources or reduce resources based on need. This is an example of what type of manageability benefit?
video.explanation: This refers to built-in cloud automation that dynamically manages resources based on demand. Cloud services handle scaling, provisioning, and maintenance, allowing businesses to focus on applications rather than infrastructure.

video.text: Your company regularly audits the usage of cloud computing resources to ensure they are in compliance with regulatory requirements and corporate standards. What practice is this an example of?
video.explanation: Governance in the cloud involves the processes, policies, and standards that ensure resources are being used appropriately and in compliance with legal and corporate requirements. Regular audits are a key part of maintaining effective governance.

video.text: Which of the following is a built-in role in Azure RBAC? Select all that apply.
video.explanation: In Azure Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), "Reader", "Owner" and "Contributor" are built-in roles. The "Reader" role allows users to view resources but not make changes. "Owner" provides full control, while "Contributor" allows users to create and manage resources but not assign roles.

video.text: Which of the following is an example of an IaaS offering from Azure?
video.explanation: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) provides virtualized computing resources over the internet. Azure Virtual Machines is a prime example because it provides virtualized compute resources that customers can use to run their workloads, including operating systems and applications, while Microsoft manages the underlying hardware.

video.text: What is the maximum number of web apps a single App Service Plan (Premium v3) can support?
video.explanation: In the Premium v3 tier of Azure App Service Plans, there is no predefined limit to the number of web apps you can host. While the plan allows for unlimited web apps, the actual number you can effectively run depends on the plan's resource capacity and the demands of your applications.

video.text: How can tags be used to optimize costs in Azure?

options.text: By automatically shutting down underutilized resources
By identifying resources that can be migrated to a lower-cost tier
By categorizing resources based on their cost and usage
By automatically applying discounts to tagged resources

video.explanation: Tags in Azure help organize resources by assigning metadata (such as cost center, environment, or department). This categorization enables better cost tracking, reporting, and optimization by identifying which resources contribute most to cloud expenses.

video.text: In which storage redundancy option does Azure keep six copies of your files across two regions?
video.explanation: Geo-Redundant Storage (GRS) keeps six copies of your data: three copies in the primary region and three more in a secondary region that is geographically distant. This setup ensures high availability and disaster recovery in case of regional failures.

video.text: Which connectivity option of Azure can provide connectivity from your on-premises corporate network into Azure over a private line, not travelling over the public Internet?
video.explanation: Azure ExpressRoute provides a private, dedicated connection between your on-premises network and Azure, bypassing the public Internet. This results in higher reliability, lower latency, and better security compared to VPN-based solutions.

video.text: What does cost predictability mean in the context of Azure?

options.text: The ability to accurately forecast future costs.
The ability to avoid unexpected charges.
The ability to allocate costs to specific resources.
The ability to reduce costs over time.

video.explanation: Cost predictability in Azure means being able to estimate and plan for future cloud expenses based on current and projected usage. This helps businesses budget effectively and avoid financial surprises when using cloud services.

video.text: What is the maximum amount of data that can be stored in a single Azure Storage account?
video.explanation: A single Azure Storage account can store up to 5 PB of data when using Locally Redundant Storage (LRS), Zone-Redundant Storage (ZRS), or Geo-Redundant Storage (GRS). This capacity allows organizations to manage large amounts of data efficiently.

video.text: What is a fault domain?

options.text: A report available through Azure Service Health
A method to resolve human-readable names into IP addresses
The place where tectonic plates meet far below the surface of the Earth
A physical grouping of servers within an Azure data center.

video.explanation: A fault domain in Azure refers to a group of servers that share a common power source and network switch within a data center. Azure Availability Sets use fault domains to ensure that virtual machines are distributed across multiple physical hardware units, reducing the risk of a single point of failure.

video.text: What is the primary purpose of single sign-on (SSO)?

options.text: To add an extra layer of security to user accounts.
To allow users to log in to multiple applications with a single set of credentials.
To prevent unauthorized access to cloud resources.

video.explanation: Single Sign-On (SSO) enables users to authenticate once and gain access to multiple applications or services without needing to log in again. It improves user experience by reducing the number of passwords to remember and enhances security by minimizing weak or reused passwords.

video.text: What is the name of the top-level management group of an organization?
video.explanation: In Azure Management Groups, the Root Management Group is the top-level management group that contains all other management groups and subscriptions in an organization. It provides a way to apply governance policies and access controls consistently across all resources.

video.text: Azure peering can connect two networks even though they belong to different subscriptions or customer accounts.
video.explanation: Azure Virtual Network Peering allows you to connect two Azure Virtual Networks (VNets), even if they belong to different subscriptions or different Azure Active Directory tenants. This enables seamless network connectivity between separate environments while maintaining low-latency and high-bandwidth connections.

video.text: Fill in the blank: ____ is a mechanism that allows you to connect two virtual networks within Azure.
video.explanation: Azure Virtual Network Peering allows you to connect two Azure virtual networks seamlessly, providing low-latency, high-bandwidth connectivity between VNets.

video.text: What is the primary purpose of Microsoft Entra ID?

options.text: To secure network traffic and protect against cyber threats
To provide on-premises domain services in the cloud
To manage user identities and access to applications and resources
To store and manage large amounts of data

video.explanation: Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is a cloud-based identity and access management service that manages user identities and controls access to applications and resources.

video.text: Which of the following is a passwordless authentication method supported by Azure?

options.text: Only biometric authentication (e.g., fingerprint, facial recognition)

video.explanation: Azure supports passwordless authentication through Windows Hello for Business (biometric) and FIDO2 security keys, plus Microsoft Authenticator phone-based authentication.

video.text: What is the primary purpose of an Azure resource group?

options.text: To group related Azure resources together for management and deployment.
To provide a logical container for Azure subscriptions.
To act as a central hub or dashboard for all Azure services.
To manage user accounts and access control.

video.explanation: An Azure resource group is a logical container that organizes and manages related Azure resources sharing the same lifecycle or purpose.

video.text: Which of the following is NOT a core capability of Microsoft Purview?
video.explanation: Microsoft Purview focuses on data governance, compliance, discovery, classification, and protection, not data migration or integration.

video.text: Which Azure service can be used to deploy and scale serverless containerized applications?
video.explanation: Azure Container Instances is a serverless container solution that deploys and scales containerized applications without managing VMs or Kubernetes clusters.

video.text: Fill in the blank: A ____ is a geographical area on the planet that contains at least one, but potentially multiple datacenters that are nearby and networked together with a low-latency network.
video.explanation: A region is a geographical area containing one or more datacenters networked together with low-latency connections.

video.text: What is the primary purpose of an availability set in Azure?

options.text: To ensure data redundancy and durability
To protect against single points of failure
To provide load balancing for web applications
To group virtual machines for easier management

video.explanation: An availability set protects VMs from single points of failure by distributing them across multiple fault domains and update domains within a datacenter.

video.text: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)?
video.explanation: With IaaS the customer manages the operating system; it is not managed by the provider, unlike PaaS where the OS is managed by the cloud provider.

video.text: What is the benefit of using Azure Virtual Desktop compared to traditional on-premises desktop virtualization solutions?
video.explanation: Azure Virtual Desktop provides improved scalability, increased security, and lower costs compared to on-premises desktop virtualization.

video.text: Which storage option should you choose if you need the absolute highest performance (regardless of the cost) for intense workloads like SAP HANA or transaction-heavy applications?
video.explanation: Azure Ultra Disks deliver the highest IOPS, throughput, and lowest latency, ideal for intensive workloads like SAP HANA and transaction-heavy applications.

video.text: Which of the following is NOT a key aspect of predictability in Azure?
video.explanation: Fault tolerance relates to reliability and availability, not predictability, which focuses on consistent performance, scalability, and cost optimization.

video.text: What is a key benefit of the consumption-based model in cloud computing?
video.explanation: The consumption-based model means you only pay for the resources you actually use, avoiding large upfront costs and scaling spending with actual needs.

video.text: Which of the following is NOT a core component of Azure's reliability strategy?
video.explanation: Azure's reliability strategy focuses on availability, fault tolerance, and redundancy; performance, while important, is not a core component of it.

video.text: Which of the following qualities is unique to Private Cloud?

options.text: A cloud infrastructure dedicated to a single organization, managed either by the organization itself or by a third-party provider
The virtual network is not accessible from the public Internet
An application that uses a network security group, firewall, distributed denial of service protection, and other network security methods
Anyone can sign up using a credit card

video.explanation: A private cloud provides exclusive resources and infrastructure dedicated to a single organization, offering greater control, customization, and security.

video.text: In which storage redundancy option does Azure give you a secondary endpoint for read-only access?
video.explanation: RA-GRS replicates data across two geographically separated regions (like GRS) and also provides a secondary read-only endpoint for high availability and disaster recovery.

video.text: How does data transfer between Azure regions impact costs?

options.text: It's charged based on the destination region only
It's charged based on the source region only
It's always free, regardless of the distance
It's charged based on the amount of data transferred and the distance

video.explanation: Data transfer between regions typically incurs egress charges; the cost depends on how much data is transferred and which regions are involved.

video.text: What is the primary benefit of using Microsoft Entra Conditional Access?

options.text: Enhanced security by limiting access to authorized users and devices.

video.explanation: Conditional Access enforces granular access controls based on conditions such as user location, device compliance, and risk level, allowing only trusted users and devices.

video.text: What is the primary benefit of using PaaS compared to IaaS?
video.explanation: PaaS reduces development time by providing a pre-configured environment with tools, frameworks, and services, without managing the underlying infrastructure.

video.text: Fill in the blank: ____ stores data offline and offers the lowest storage costs.
video.explanation: Archive storage stores data offline and offers the lowest storage costs, ideal for rarely accessed data retained for long-term storage.

video.text: Which Azure Storage access tier is optimized (including for cost) for data accessed infrequently and must be stored for at least 30 days?
video.explanation: The Cool access tier is optimized for infrequently accessed data stored for at least 30 days, offering lower storage costs than the Hot tier.

video.text: Which feature of Azure Storage makes it durable?
video.explanation: Redundancy ensures data durability by keeping multiple copies of data across different locations or storage types, protecting against data loss.

video.text: What is the primary purpose of tags in Azure?

options.text: To categorize and organize resources for better management
To assign security permissions to resources

video.explanation: Tags categorize and organize resources via key-value metadata, helping with resource management, cost tracking, and grouping for reporting and automation.

video.text: Which of the following best describes scalability in the cloud?

options.text: The ability to reduce costs by limiting storage
The ability to increase or decrease resources based on demand
The ability to run applications without an internet connection

video.explanation: Scalability in the cloud is the ability to adjust resources based on changing demand, handling varying workloads without over- or under-provisioning.

video.text: What is the primary purpose of Azure RBAC?

options.text: To protect against unauthorized access to Azure subscriptions.
To grant users the appropriate level of access to Azure resources.

video.explanation: Azure Role-Based Access Control manages access to Azure resources, assigning specific permissions so users have the minimum access required for their tasks.

video.text: What is the minimum number of Availability Zones required to create a highly available application in Azure?
video.explanation: At least two Availability Zones are required for a highly available application, protecting it from failure in a single zone.

video.text: Which of the following is a benefit of using sovereign regions in Azure?
video.explanation: Sovereign regions help organizations meet specific legal, regulatory, and compliance requirements, reducing compliance risks around data residency and sovereignty.

video.text: What is the primary difference between pay-as-you-go and reserved instance pricing models in the cloud?

options.text: Reserved instances offer higher performance than pay-as-you-go instances.
Reserved instances offer discounted rates for long-term commitments, while pay-as-you-go is billed based on usage.
Pay-as-you-go requires upfront payment, while reserved instances are billed hourly.
Pay-as-you-go is only available for public cloud models, while reserved instances are for private cloud models.

video.explanation: Pay-as-you-go charges based on usage with no commitment; reserved instances commit to specific resources for one or three years in exchange for a discounted rate.

video.text: Which of the following benefits are provided by Azure ExpressRoute compared to a regular Site-to-Site VPN? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Data travels over a private network, not a public one
Access to private Virtual Networks that do not have devices with a public IP address

video.explanation: ExpressRoute offers a private, dedicated connection (not over the public internet) that typically delivers faster and more consistent performance than a Site-to-Site VPN.

video.text: Why are Azure datacenters located in various regions around the world?

options.text: To ensure redundancy and high availability.

video.explanation: Azure datacenters span regions to comply with local regulations, reduce latency by placing resources closer to users, and ensure redundancy and high availability.

video.text: What is the primary advantage of using Azure's built-in security features compared to managing security on-premises?
video.explanation: Azure's built-in security features reduce the need for specialized in-house expertise, providing automated tools for threat detection, encryption, and access control.

video.text: Which compute type offers the greatest flexibility and control over the underlying hardware, allowing you to customize the environment to your specific needs?
video.explanation: Virtual Machines offer the greatest flexibility and control, letting you select the OS, configure hardware, and install software, ideal for specific or legacy configurations.

video.text: What type of scaling typically involves moving from a smaller machine to a larger (more powerful) machine?
video.explanation: Vertical scaling involves moving to a larger, more powerful machine by increasing CPU, RAM, or storage of a single server.

video.text: Which tool lets you centralize your file shares in Azure Files and keep the flexibility, performance, and compatibility of a Windows file server?
video.explanation: Azure File Sync centralizes file shares in Azure Files while keeping the flexibility and compatibility of a Windows file server, syncing on-premises Windows Server with Azure File shares.

video.text: Can resource groups be nested?
video.explanation: Resource groups cannot be nested. Each resource group is a container for resources but cannot contain other resource groups.

video.text: What is the primary purpose of a virtual machine scale set in Azure?

options.text: To group virtual machines for easier management
To provide load balancing for web applications
To automatically scale virtual machines based on demand
To ensure data redundancy and durability

video.explanation: A virtual machine scale set automatically scales the number of VMs up or down based on demand, metrics, or schedules, providing high availability.

video.text: What entities can management groups contain?
video.explanation: Management groups organize and manage multiple subscriptions, applying policies and access controls across them; they contain subscriptions, not individual resources or resource groups.

video.text: Which Azure App Service hosting option would you choose if you wanted isolated hardware and network, ensuring they are not used by any other Azure customers?
video.explanation: An App Service Environment provides an isolated, fully managed environment with network isolation and dedicated hardware not shared with other Azure customers.

video.text: Which of the following is the most likely scenario in which to choose Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) options in cloud computing?

options.text: Someone looking to run an app for free in the cloud
Someone looking to reduce administrative overhead

video.explanation: Lift-and-shift migration moves existing on-premises workloads to the cloud with minimal changes, for which IaaS is ideal.

video.text: What is the key characteristic of serverless computing that distinguishes it from traditional infrastructure?
video.explanation: Serverless computing automatically scales resources based on workload without the user managing the underlying infrastructure.

video.text: You have a virtual machine that you need to have a public endpoint - accessible from the Internet. Which of the following resources do you need to have in order to achieve your goal?
video.explanation: To make a VM accessible from the internet you must assign it a public IP address, giving it a public endpoint accessible externally.

video.text: Fill in the blank: Cloud computing is a model of delivering IT services such as computing, networking and storage over the Internet on a ____ basis.

options.text: pay up-front as a capital expense

video.explanation: Cloud computing delivers IT services over the internet on a pay-as-you-go basis, paying only for the resources you use.

video.text: Which of the following is NOT a key component of Zero Trust security?
video.explanation: Zero Trust focuses on micro-segmentation, least privilege access, and continuous monitoring; strong passwords, while useful, are not a core component.

video.text: What is the default storage account type used by AzCopy?
video.explanation: AzCopy works with Blob storage by default and is commonly used to transfer data to and from Azure Blob Storage.

video.text: What is the primary benefit of high availability in cloud computing?

options.text: Minimizes downtime and ensures continuous service

video.explanation: High availability minimizes downtime and ensures continuous service, typically via redundant resources and failover mechanisms.

video.text: Which of the following is a key difference between Azure B2B and Azure B2C?

options.text: B2B is for internal users, while B2C is for external users.
B2B is for cloud-based applications, while B2C is for on-premises applications.
B2B is for business-to-business collaboration, while B2C is for business-to-customer interactions.
There is no significant difference between the two services.

video.explanation: Azure B2B enables secure resource sharing with external partner organizations, while Azure B2C manages access for external customers (business-to-consumer).

video.text: A small startup with limited IT resources and a need for flexible scalability would be best suited for which cloud model?
video.explanation: The public cloud provides on-demand resources, cost efficiency, and scalability without managing physical infrastructure, ideal for a small startup.

video.text: What are the two types of manageability for cloud computing? (Select all that apply.)
video.explanation: Management of the cloud refers to managing the underlying infrastructure and services; management in the cloud refers to managing the applications, data, and services hosted within the cloud.

video.text: According to the shared responsibility model, who is responsible for keeping the guest operating system (Windows or Linux) updated on an Azure Virtual Machine?

options.text: It's actually automatically taken care of, and no one needs to do anything
The cloud provider, in this case Microsoft Azure

video.explanation: Under the shared responsibility model, the customer is responsible for managing and updating the guest OS on Azure VMs; Microsoft handles the physical hardware, network, and infrastructure.

video.text: Fill in the blank: ____ refers to the policies, processes, and controls that organizations implement to ensure that their cloud computing initiatives align with their overall business objectives and risk management strategies.
video.explanation: Governance refers to the policies, processes, and controls ensuring cloud initiatives align with business objectives and risk management, supporting compliance and risk management.
